blocks.title: After this PDF you can
bullets: say my, your, his, her, our and their correctly
point out things with este, ese and aquel
use pronouns after a preposition (para mí, conmigo)
ask all the basic questions: what, who, where, when, how, how much, which, why

blocks.text: Possessives go before the noun and agree with the thing owned, not with the owner: mi hermano, mis hermanas. Only nuestro and vuestro also change for gender.

blocks.title: One word, many owners: su
blocks.text: su can mean his, her, your (formal) or their. If it is unclear, say who: la casa de él, la casa de ella, la casa de ustedes, la casa de ellos. Also note: tu (your) has no accent, but tú (you) does.
2. Demonstratives: this, that, that over there

head: Distance
m. sing.
f. sing.
m. / f. pl.
Place word
rows: far from both (that, those over there)

items: They agree with the noun: este libro, esta casa, estos libros, estas casas.
esto, eso, aquello are neutral. Use them for an unknown thing or an idea: ¿Qué es esto? Eso es verdad.
Spanish has three distances, Dutch has two (dit / dat). ese is “that, near you”, aquel is “that, far away”.

blocks.text: Este coche es nuevo, ese coche es viejo y aquel coche es muy caro. (This car is new, that car is old and that car over there is very expensive.)

head: Person
After a preposition
Example
rows: Voy con él. Hablo de ella.

blocks.title: Two special forms
blocks.text: con + mí = conmigo and con + ti = contigo: ¿Vienes conmigo? Sí, voy contigo. Never write con mí or con ti. After para, a, de, en and sin use mí and ti, not yo and tú.
Question words always carry a written accent and the whole question is wrapped in ¿ ?.

items: cuánto agrees with the noun that follows: ¿Cuánta agua? ¿Cuántas personas?
qué or cuál? Use qué es to ask for a definition (¿Qué es esto?) and qué + noun to choose (¿Qué libro prefieres?). Use cuál es to ask for a specific piece of information (¿Cuál es tu número?).
por qué (two words, accent) asks why?. porque (one word, no accent) answers because: ¿Por qué estudias español? Porque quiero viajar.

rows: A possessive agrees with the noun, so plural nouns take mis, tus, sus.
Nuestro and vuestro also change for gender.
A question uses the two-word form por qué. Porque (one word) answers.
Cuánto agrees with años and carries an accent.
After a preposition use mí, not yo.
